Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, and then Jordan will do a 1-line goal, is that ok?
[00:10] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Yep, goal is to align on renewal ask, confirm EU private pilot scope, and list sec docs next steps.
[00:18] Maya (Hawthorn): Thanks, yep that's what we want. Our previous commit ends in Dec, looking to lock in something early Nov. Need a ~2x uplift for EU region and we have stricter residency for EU clinical data.
[00:32] Tomasz (Hawthorn): We also need to understand latency guarantees — some endpoints are customer-facing and 99th pct needs to be under 300ms if possible.
[00:42] Priya (Redwood SE): Understood. For model and sequence mix, we can profile batching to hit that but for 99p under 300ms typically we recommend a dedicated pool or private nodes in-region; hosted can do it but you see some tail variance.
[00:58] Liam (Hawthorn): Quick Q: when you say private nodes in-region, is that fully customer-managed or Redwood-managed VPC? We need clarity for compliance.
[01:08] Evan (Redwood): Good question. We have a Private deployment option: control plane can be customer-managed in your VPC and you can use your KMS. Redwood can also offer a managed VPC where we handle infra but keys still in your KMS — there are tradeoffs.
[01:26] Sofia (Hawthorn Security): Important — keys must be customer controlled; HSM preferred, and we need audit logging retained 3 years. Do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[01:36] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Private mode. Audit log retention is configurable; default is 90 days but enterprise add-on can extend. We'll share exact retention options in the security pack.
[01:50] Maya (Hawthorn): Another thing: we run multiple models — some small, some larger. Are there recommended quantization options or variants to lower cost without losing clinical output quality?
[02:04] Priya (Redwood SE): We can suggest quantization profiles per-model. Also automatic fallback policies help: lower-cost variant for non-critical routes. But we should validate in evals so there's no QA/regression.
[02:18] Tomasz (Hawthorn): Can Redwood run an eval job on sample prompts? We'd like to see baseline quality and perf delta.
[02:24] Evan (Redwood): Absolutely. Next steps include a perf/quality bench on your sample prompt set. If you can share payloads, Priya will run a profiling pass.
[02:36] Liam (Hawthorn): We'll provide sample payload distribution — avg seq length, percent embeddings, peak qps windows.
[02:44] Evan (Redwood): Great. On pricing, for renewals we can propose a 6-month uplift ahead of the annual, or lock an annual commit with tiered regional activation. For EU private nodes there's an extra infra fee — we'll send a matrix.
[02:58] Maya (Hawthorn): We'd prefer short commit (6 months) while we validate on-prem pilot. Also need failover: if EU nodes go down, can traffic route to hosted fallback in another region without breaching residency rules?
[03:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Failover is policy driven. We can set route-by-policy where only non-sensitive routes failover; anything flagged sensitive stays in-region. Need to map route tags.
[03:24] Sofia (Hawthorn): How about compliance evidence — SOC2, ISO certs? We need copies for procurement.
[03:30] Evan (Redwood): We'll share SOC2 and ISO attestations, penetration test summary, and a KMS/HSM integration note.
[03:38] Tomasz (Hawthorn): Can we also get an architecture diagram for the private deployment showing network flow and egress points?
[03:44] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, I'll attach a network diagram and the checklist for ports, peering, IPs.
[03:50] Evan (Redwood): On benchmarking, Priya will run a profiling pass once we get sample payloads. Expect two runs: standard throughput and tail-latency targeted runs. We'll include KV cache warmup to show best-case perf.
[04:04] Liam (Hawthorn): Slightly worried about transcription: oh, sorry — I mean cold start times. How do you handle model cold starts during scale up?
[04:10] Priya (Redwood SE): We do warm pools and continuous batching; model warmup and KV cache reuse reduces cold-starts. For private nodes we can also pin hot model shards.
[04:22] Maya (Hawthorn): Competitor question — any features Redwood lacks vs Anthropic or Bedrock for on-prem?
[04:28] Evan (Redwood): We compete on operational controls and observability; Bedrock has native cloud integrations but less private on-prem play. Anthropic focuses on model safety — worth a separate convo.
[04:38] Tomasz (Hawthorn): Ok. On contract language: can we get a short-form amendment to extend current term by 6 months and add a private pilot clause?
[04:47] Evan (Redwood): We can draft an amendment. Jordan will own the contract language.
[04:52] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Yep I'll prepare a redline for the amendment and send to Maya and legal.
[04:58] Sofia (Hawthorn Security): Also need commitments on data purging and data access policy for the pilot.
[05:04] Priya (Redwood SE): We'll include data lifecycle notes; by default logs are redacted, and we can set stricter retention for your org.
[05:12] Evan (Redwood): Let me recap next steps quickly: Redwood will send pricing matrix and private pilot cost, SOC2 and KMS/HSM notes, network diagram, and Priya will draft the tech checklist and run perf once payload samples are in. Customer will share payloads, encryption requirements, and confirm SLOs.
[05:32] Maya (Hawthorn): That matches our expectations. We aim to decide the uplift by Oct 28 so timeline looks tight but achievable.
[05:42] Evan (Redwood): Great — we'll target sending the docs by Oct 24 so you have time to review.
[05:48] Tomasz (Hawthorn): One last micro ask: can Redwood include an example of rollback policy for model regressions?
[05:55] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll include a canary/rollback example and the eval gate thresholds.
[06:02] Evan (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the attachments and set the pilot kickoff tentative for the week of Nov 3.

Meeting end.
